Oracle Fusion Cloud 26D: what changed

136 changes we track: the most relevant ones, up to 25 per module family (out of 768 features, by our count, in the 26D What's New documents for Financials, Procurement, SCM, Logistics, Projects and HCM). See the 26D what-to-test checklist →

Impact on upgrade is our editorial rating of how much a change affects existing users and testing; Oracle scale is Oracle's own rating. Always confirm details on the linked Oracle page.

By module family: Financials (25) · HCM (25) · Logistics (OTM, GTM, WMS) (25) · Procurement (25) · Project Management (11) · Supply Chain & Manufacturing (25) · Former opt-ins now standard in 26D (23)

Get the 26D checklist now: what switches on by itself, which former opt-ins are now standard, what to test

Inside the free 26D checklist (PDF):

  • The 23 opt-ins Oracle lists as ending with 26D: 9 switch on for everyone, 14 need setup
  • 9 HCM Redwood default switches and other HCM notices for 26D
  • 9 baseline regression checks, plus typical 26D test and production dates by cohort

Then one plain-English email per Oracle quarterly update, linked to Oracle's docs. Free. 4 emails a year plus short opt-in alerts. Unsubscribe anytime. Read issue #1 (26C) → · Privacy

Payables Period Close Workspace

Impact on upgrade: mediumOracle scale: Larger scaleAutomatically onFinancialsFinancials · Payables AgentAgentic app
Use the Payables Period Close Workspace to achieve a timely, controlled, and explainable Payables close. For the selected ledger and accounting period, the workspace brings together invoice, payment, and period status to establish the current close posture, identify what is preventing progress, and direct attention to the work that matters most.
Oracle's "Impact to Existing Processes": Larger scale · Action to enable: None · Oracle source
